transcript.text: I need to flag a security issue I found this afternoon while debugging an unrelated authentication issue. I confirmed that two customer tenants can use the same project slug. This means our current unscoped project-key cache policy could return one tenant's recommendation response to another tenant — a cross-tenant data leak. My application recommendation is to use a cache key containing both tenant ID and project key, and to require a security isolation test before launch. I haven't filed this finding yet, but given the launch is tomorrow morning, I'm raising it now.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: During a failover rehearsal this morning, I measured that DNS and service recovery take 12 minutes, while the origin database's protection limit permits serving cached responses for exactly 20 minutes before requests must stop. Because the 20-minute limit covers the measured recovery period, my reliability recommendation is to serve stale cached responses during an origin outage with a maximum stale window of exactly 20 minutes. I haven't updated the launch runbook yet.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Final production caching policy will use a cache key scoped to both tenant ID and project key, replacing the default unscoped project-key cache policy.
A security isolation test verifying cross-tenant cache separation must be completed and passed before launch.
Failover mode set to serve stale cached responses during origin outage with a maximum stale window of 20 minutes, matching the origin database protection limit.
Launch runbook must be updated to reflect the serve-stale failover mode and 20-minute max stale window before sign-off.
Application sign-off contingent on security isolation test passing.
Reliability sign-off contingent on runbook update reflecting the 20-minute serve-stale failover policy.
